parallel.requirements: The parallel parent and workflow recognized ESM-only Node.js, zero external dependencies, hand-written argparse, UTF-8 byte lengths, Python bytes repr, AES-CBC chaining, and the required /output/test7.mjs entry.
parallel.plan_and_ownership: The parent delegated nearly the whole job to a workflow split into pybytes, argparse, and AES spec tracks, matching implementation tracks, then a later integration agent, verifier fan-out, triage, fix, and final-gate sequence.
parallel.implementation: Children produced several library modules: py-errors.mjs, python-bytes.mjs, argparse.mjs, aes-tables.mjs, aes-core.mjs, aes-modes.mjs, and pyaes.mjs. The entry point was assigned to a later integration phase that never ran.
parallel.integration_and_delivery: The workflow was killed with no integration result. Artifact validation copied only library files and explicitly did not find the expected test7.mjs entry.
parallel.verification: Component children ran many oracle probes and some local harnesses, including bytes, argparse, AES vectors, and small fuzz checks, but the planned integrated verifier and final gate were never reached.
parallel.unfinished_or_incorrect: At closure the parent had no final response, no assembled entry point, two implementation children still in progress, and a 0/28 official evaluation.

serial.requirements: The serial agent recognized the same required CLI flags, ESM .mjs output, no external dependencies, UTF-8 encoding, Python bytes repr, AES key-size behavior, CBC chaining, and /output/test7.mjs delivery.
serial.plan_and_ownership: The serial agent kept ownership of exploration, module implementation, entry-point assembly, differential testing, fixes, and final delivery without delegating work to subagents.
serial.implementation: It wrote pyerrors, pybytes, AES/GF/CBC modules, pyaes exports, argparse, and test7.mjs, then rewrote argparse after fuzzing exposed dash-prefixed and separator divergences.
serial.integration_and_delivery: It created the expected /output/test7.mjs entry and a coherent /output/lib tree; artifact validation reported the expected entry present.
serial.verification: It ran the sample case, a 482-case differential suite, an 800-case fuzz suite, FIPS AES vectors, and import/forbidden-pattern audits before final response.
serial.unfinished_or_incorrect: Despite stronger delivery, the official evaluator still marked solution_passed false with only 5/28 passing, indicating ordinary implementation incompleteness beyond the parallel coordination issue.

comparison_dimensions.parallel_summary: Parallel recognized the full migration target and encoded detailed task rules inside the workflow, including exact CLI, ESM, AES, and output obligations.
comparison_dimensions.serial_summary: Serial worked from the same prompt and probed the same CLI, AES, error, and formatting behavior directly.
comparison_dimensions.difference: Requirement recognition was broadly similar; the material difference was not task comprehension but whether those requirements reached a final assembled entry point.

comparison_dimensions.parallel_summary: Parallel decomposed into multiple spec and implementation child tracks and deferred entry assembly to a later integration agent after all library tracks completed.
comparison_dimensions.serial_summary: Serial kept all ownership in one agent and moved from behavior probing to module creation, entry file creation, differential fixes, and final review.
comparison_dimensions.difference: Parallel introduced a large dependency pipeline, while serial used a single-owner path that reached the entry-point step.

comparison_dimensions.parallel_summary: Parallel supplied a fixed module interface contract for child work, reducing interface ambiguity, but those child outputs still depended on a later integration phase.
comparison_dimensions.serial_summary: Serial maintained interface knowledge locally while writing imports and exports into one coherent module tree and test entry.
comparison_dimensions.difference: Parallel context was explicit but split across handoffs and an unreached integration boundary; serial avoided that handoff boundary by directly editing and reviewing the files.

comparison_dimensions.parallel_summary: Parallel children created several libraries and ran component checks, but no child or parent produced the required entry file before timeout.
comparison_dimensions.serial_summary: Serial wrote all libraries plus /output/test7.mjs, then iterated on argparse until local differential testing matched many probed cases.
comparison_dimensions.difference: The concrete implementation gap is the entry point and full assembly: serial created it, parallel did not.

comparison_dimensions.parallel_summary: Some spec and pybytes child results returned, but argparse and AES implementation children remained in progress and the workflow produced no integration result before being killed.
comparison_dimensions.serial_summary: Serial had no child result lifecycle and kept local results immediately available for subsequent edits and tests.
comparison_dimensions.difference: Parallel was blocked on unretrieved unfinished child-workflow state; serial did not depend on asynchronous result collection.

comparison_dimensions.parallel_summary: Parallel children wrote shared /output library files, but the workflow never entered the integration phase that would read those modules and write /output/test7.mjs.
comparison_dimensions.serial_summary: Serial assembled the expected entry and module tree in /output, with artifact validation confirming test7.mjs and its libraries.
comparison_dimensions.difference: There is no proven write collision; the important difference is that parallel shared-state outputs remained unassembled, while serial converted them into a packaged artifact.

comparison_dimensions.parallel_summary: Parallel gathered extensive component-level evidence inside children, but the planned integrated verifier fan-out and final gate did not run after integration because integration never started.
comparison_dimensions.serial_summary: Serial ran sample checks, a 482-case differential suite, an 800-case fuzz suite, FIPS AES vectors, and import/forbidden-pattern audits before final response.
comparison_dimensions.difference: Serial closed a local whole-program verification loop; parallel only accumulated partial component checks and then failed official evaluation with no entry point.

comparison_dimensions.parallel_summary: Parallel consumed essentially the full 2400-second cell budget, returned code 143, timed out, and left no final response.
comparison_dimensions.serial_summary: Serial completed normally in 1681.523 agent seconds with returncode 0 and about 715 seconds of remaining retry budget.
comparison_dimensions.difference: Parallel closure was forced by timeout before assembly; serial reached a normal final response and packaged artifact despite failing the official pass threshold.

outcome_analysis.explanation: The current completed official evaluations make this a both_fail pair: parallel solution_passed is false at 0/28 and serial solution_passed is false at 5/28. The concrete task-solving difference is still substantial. Parallel consumed the run in a broad workflow and was killed before the integration phase could create /output/test7.mjs; artifact validation therefore found only library files and no expected entry. Serial completed a single-agent implementation path, wrote test7.mjs, ran multiple local verification loops, and artifact validation accepted the entry, but its implementation remained incomplete enough to pass only five official samples.
parallel_contributors: The broad workflow split specification, implementation, integration, verification, triage, fixes, and final gate across child agents and was killed before integration.
The required entry file was never produced, so official artifact validation failed before any functional parity could be demonstrated.
serial_contributors: The serial agent kept ownership of entry assembly and produced /output/test7.mjs plus libraries.
The serial agent fixed discovered argparse divergences and ran differential, fuzz, FIPS, and import-compliance checks before final response.
ordinary_implementation_differences: Serial's delivered code was still only partially correct under the official hidden tests, passing 5/28 rather than the pass threshold.
Parallel's missing entry artifact is a delivery failure caused by workflow completion, not an ordinary AES or argparse code defect visible in a completed program.
outcome_analysis.causal_scope: supported comparative contributors, not an exclusive root cause

candidates.reason: Implementation ownership existed through pybytes, argparse, and AES implementation children; the problem was that the workflow did not finish, not that implementation was unassigned.
The workflow explicitly assigned an integration agent to read library modules and write test7.mjs; it simply never reached that phase.
The required entry point was assigned to the integration phase, so assembly was owned even though that phase was not reached before timeout.
The parent made the workflow responsible for the end-to-end pipeline; the observed defect is budget exhaustion in that pipeline rather than lack of an owner.
The workflow did not block all work behind one mandatory preflight; several spec and implementation children ran in overlapping phases.
Investigation was not completed as a wholly serial first phase; implementation children began as track specs completed, and the adverse outcome came from workflow breadth and timeout.
The indispensable entry assembly started too late because the overall fan-out pipeline exhausted budget; there is no separate auxiliary-work allocation episode more specific than fan-out exhaustion.
The workflow fanned out spec, implementation, planned verification, triage, fixes, and final gate work, retried a stalled spec child, and was killed before integration could assemble the deliverable.
candidates.realized_consequence: The integration and final-gate phases never executed, /output/test7.mjs was absent from the copied artifact, and official evaluation recorded 0/28.
candidates.near_match_reason: Although the overall workflow was large, the observed budget loss came from collective multi-track fan-out and retry/stall behavior rather than one child with a single overbroad task.

candidates.reason: No single child assignment is the best explanation; the failure came from a broad workflow with multiple tracks and active children consuming the shared deadline.
Child prompts included the mission rules and relevant task obligations; there is no evidenced known requirement omitted from a child brief that made returned work unusable.
The workflow defined explicit module paths and exported names for each separately owned component, and no incompatibility between completed components was adjudicated before timeout.
No known finding is shown to disappear during transfer; spec outputs were either used in implementation prompts or the pipeline ended before a receiver could act.
Some child reports were long, but there is no decision point where an available bulky handoff was too large to consume and caused wrong integration.
No receiver acted on a superseded workspace, requirement, dependency, or decision state; the pipeline stalled before integration decisions occurred.
The ledger does not show incompatible child reports both reaching the parent and remaining unadjudicated at an integration decision.
The parallel parent made no observable whole-task completion or acceptance decision; final.txt is empty and closure was forced by timeout.
The AES spec retry repeated some probing after a stalled attempt, but this is treated as part of the retained fan-out budget episode rather than a separate retained retry pattern.

There was no earlier completed child failure that the parent could take over; the workflow failure happened at the same deadline that ended the parent run.
Returned spec and pybytes results were not contradicted or ignored at a decision point; the workflow failed before the dependent integration decision.
The parent made periodic progress checks, and the timeout is already accounted for as fan-out budget exhaustion rather than an independent blind-wait episode.
The children wrote different library files according to the interface contract; there is no competing design collision that reached reconciliation.

retained_patterns.reason: The parallel workflow fanned out across multiple spec and implementation children and planned additional verifier, triage, fix, and final-gate phases. It exhausted the finite cell budget before integration, leaving no entry artifact.
retained_patterns.realized_consequence: Integration and final-gate phases never executed, the expected /output/test7.mjs entry was absent, and the official evaluator recorded 0/28.
retained_patterns.near_match_reason: The observable failure was collective fan-out and retry/stall budget exhaustion, not a single overbroad child task with a separately correctable scope.
